title: Chapter 14 — The Man Who Already Knew

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 14
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Man Who Already Knew
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Collector found them before they finished packing for the east-side survey.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He was waiting in the narrow lane behind the cheap room, leaning against the wall like a man who had all morning and no intention of wasting it on politeness. Two temple guards stood a short distance away, looking bored in the specific way of men paid to look dangerous. The Collector himself looked almost regretful. That bothered Zeek more than anger would have.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: You've been busy,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the Collector said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's hand drifted toward the haft of his axe and then stopped. En-HEH-doo's expression went carefully blank. Ninsun simply watched, stylus still in her fingers from the map she had been updating.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek set the pack down.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We're taking a paying job. East side. Walls that need measuring. Nothing that should interest you.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: Everything you do interests me lately.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Collector's eyes moved across the four of them, lingering a fraction too long on the linen around Zeek's left hand and the satchel where Ninsun kept her scraps.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: Notches in walls that officially don't exist. Questions about blank tablets. A certain district that keeps appearing on no one's maps but yours. You've drawn attention.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: From who?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg asked.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Collector almost smiled.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: From people who prefer their attention not to be noticed in return.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo tilted her head.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You're not here to buy.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked at Zeek.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: I'm here because your father made the same mistake you're making now. He thought the City was a puzzle that wanted to be solved. It isn't. It's a lid. And lids exist to keep something from rising. The more you mark it, the more you tell it exactly where the curious ones are standing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's voice was quiet.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You know about the marks.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: I know about the ones who made them before you. Most of them stopped. A few didn't. The ones who didn't are why certain drawers in the lower archives stay locked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He glanced at the two guards, then back.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: I'm offering you the same chance I offered your father. Walk away from the shifted streets. Take the east-side work. Take the silver. Let the lid stay closed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek held his stare.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: And if we don't?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Collector's expression didn't change.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: Then you'll learn, the same way he did, that some prices are paid in advance. And some debts collect themselves.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He pushed off the wall, adjusted the sleeve of his robe, and walked away. The guards fell in behind him without being told. At the end of the lane he paused, just long enough to look back once.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: Your father finally understood he had been asking the wrong question,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Collector
lines.text: I hope you're smarter than he was. Or luckier. I'm not certain which one matters more.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The lane felt smaller after he left.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg exhaled through his nose.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I fucking hate that man.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: He's not wrong about the attention,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo said. She was already recalculating something behind her eyes.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: We've been loud in places that prefer quiet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun looked down at the map still half-open in her hands. The boxes labeled CLAIMED, COST, and LIMIT sat in a tight cluster near the tanners' row.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: He knew about the marks. He knew about the ones who came before us. That means the locked drawers have names in them. Or the absence of names.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek picked up the pack. The journal inside it had not been opened in nine days. The decision still felt like the only clean thing he owned.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We take the east-side job,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We get paid. We watch who watches us. And we don't cut another notch until we know whether the Collector is warning us or herding us.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one argued.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They walked out of the lane in the order that had become habit. Behind them the cheap room and the map and the accumulating scraps of evidence waited like a second set of lungs the city had not yet decided to collapse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ahead, the ordinary noise of Uruk continued—merchants, animals, arguments that had nothing to do with lids or locked drawers or the kind of debts that collected themselves.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek flexed his left hand inside the linen. The mark was warm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not look back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The east-side walls were exactly as boring as the contract promised.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three hundred cubits of mud-brick curtain wall, two collapsed towers, and a stretch of foundation that had been patched so many times the original line was anybody's guess. The temple clerk who hired them wanted measurements, load assessments, and a written recommendation on whether the whole section needed tearing down before the next flood season. Nothing shifted. Nothing breathed cooler air. Nothing carried notches.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was the most restful work they had done in weeks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg walked the foundation with a measuring rod and a piece of chalk, marking every place the brick had settled more than a finger's width. En-HEH-doo counted and sorted the reusable stone the way other people counted coin. Ninsun copied the older survey marks still visible on the inner face—temple codes, old ownership seals, the usual bureaucratic scars. Zeek checked the places where later repairs had been cut into earlier ones, reading the sequence the way his father had taught him to read mortar.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He paused halfway along the inner wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One repair interrupted another.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then another.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three different masons.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Three different clay mixes.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The oldest repair had been careful. Tight joints. Fired brick cut to match the original courses.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The second had simply filled cracks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The newest had hidden both.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg noticed him stop.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Someone kept fixing the same place.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Bad foundation?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek brushed away another layer of dust.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: If it were structural, they'd replace the whole course.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: So?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: They only repaired this section.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo joined them.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Meaning?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: They weren't trying to save the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He traced the line of repairs with one finger.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: They were trying to hide something inside it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked at the perfectly ordinary brickwork.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You can tell that from mud?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I can tell someone paid for three repairs where one would've done.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He smiled faintly.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: People rarely waste labor without a reason.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For most of the morning no one spoke about lids or locked drawers or the Collector's quiet threat. The ordinary work was enough.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Near midday Ninsun stopped in front of a section of inner wall that looked no different from the rest. She ran her fingers along a line of faded wedge marks, then crouched and brushed dust from a deeper cut near the base.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun crouched beside the repaired section.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Zeek.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He came over. The others followed without being called.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: There's writing here.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I don't see anything.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You aren't meant to.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She dampened one corner of her sleeve and wiped gently across the brick.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The dust disappeared.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nothing else happened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then sunlight shifted behind a passing cloud.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The shallow cuts suddenly caught the light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo sucked in a breath.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I see it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Barely.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The survey marks had been cut so shallow they disappeared unless viewed from exactly the right angle.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek knelt beside them.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: They expected later repairs.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: What?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: They carved them after the wall was finished.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He pointed.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: If these were construction marks, they'd be beneath this plaster.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Instead they sat on top of it.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: They wanted someone to erase them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg frowned.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That's a strange thing to want.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's voice was almost a whisper.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It's a very ordinary thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They all looked at her.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: History is easier to hide when you know exactly where someone will try.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She continued cleaning.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Slowly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One wedge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Another.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then the spiral.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not scratched.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not painted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Deliberately carved.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then attacked with a chisel.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The damage had broken the symbol but not destroyed it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Whoever erased it had worked angrily.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Or hurriedly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek touched the deepest cut.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: They came back.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: How do you know?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: The scoring crosses weathering.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked up.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: The wall aged.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Then somebody returned years later just to erase this.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Silence.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked around the empty survey site.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I dislike the amount of effort strangers keep spending on old bricks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The marks were old temple survey code, the kind used for private boundary work rather than public walls. Most of it was routine. One cluster near the bottom was not. The same spiral-drop that lived under the linen on Zeek's hand had been cut into the brick and then deliberately defaced—scored through so hard the chisel had split the face of the course.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beside it, in a tighter hand, three signs remained legible.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's voice had gone flat.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That's the same seal language as the broken piece we pulled from the shifted chamber. And the name under it—

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She stopped, then finished quietly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It's the uncrossed name. The one from the basin. The ordinary one. The potter or the dock worker or whoever the city decided wasn't worth erasing completely.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stared at the defaced symbol.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: So the same mark shows up on a royal tomb, a shifted street, and a temple curtain wall that officially has nothing to do with either.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: And on an ordinary person's name the city only half-deleted,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo said. She was already looking at the surrounding courses for anything else worth taking.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: That's not coincidence. That's inventory.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek ran his thumb across the scored spiral. The edges were old. Whoever had tried to erase it had done the work years ago, maybe decades. The wall had simply kept the evidence the way walls kept everything else—without comment, without loyalty, without any interest in whether the people who came later were ready to see it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun was already copying the cluster onto a fresh scrap, her handwriting smaller and tighter than usual.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The Collector said the locked drawers hold the ones who didn't stop. What if they also hold the names the city tried to cross out and couldn't quite finish?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one answered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They finished the survey because the contract required it and because leaving early would have told anyone watching that they had found something worth finding. BAH-lahg completed his measurements. En-HEH-doo stacked the reusable stone. Zeek wrote the load assessment in the dry, practical language the temple clerks preferred. Ninsun kept the new copy of the defaced seal and the half-erased name folded inside her map, separate from the rest.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By late afternoon the work was done. The clerk paid them in full and did not ask why they had spent so long on one short section of wall. They walked back toward the lower districts in the order that had become habit, four people carrying an ordinary day's pay and one more piece of proof that the city's erasures were never as complete as it wanted them to be.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek flexed his left hand beneath the linen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark remained quiet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not because nothing had happened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Because whatever lay beneath the city no longer needed to call him every day.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It already knew where he was going.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He thought about the Collector.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: About the locked drawers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: About the wall someone had repaired three separate times simply to hide one damaged symbol and one ordinary name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Collector had said his father eventually learned he had been asking the wrong question.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Walking home through the evening crowds, Zeek realized he had never asked what that question had been.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first time since opening the tomb, that frightened him more than the answer.
